* This paper doesn't focus on plant populations specifically, but the general idea is that population growth rate decreases as density increases. How might density dependence manifest in your system? (e.g. disease, resource limitation, thinning/space limitation?)

* "Inverse density dependence" is more commonly called positive density dependence. What would be an example of positive density dependence in plant populations? When might this occur?

* The authors talk about density-dependent and density-independent models or factors. What are some density-independent factors (including ones we've already talked about in this class)?

* Figure 4 shows how you could detect density-dependent and density-independent factors in experiments. Have you done experiments or seen papers that have manipulated resources and density simultaneously? Any questions about this idea of interaction effects?
